questions.questionText: What is a key condition for effective price discrimination?

options.A: The product cannot be resold to another consumer.
options.B: The product must be price inelastic.
options.C: The profits from one market can be used to subsidise another market.
options.D: There are low barriers to entry into the market.

questions.questionText: How is dynamic efficiency represented on a diagram?

options.A: a downward move to the minimum point of a long-run average cost curve
options.B: a downward shift in the long-run average cost curve
options.C: a move from a point inside a production possibility curve to a point on it
options.D: a reduction in marginal revenue so that it equals long-run marginal cost

questions.questionText: A city council is considering building a passenger terminal at its port so that the city can benefit from large cruise ships that could then dock there. It undertakes a cost–benefit analysis. What would be included as an external cost in the city council’s cost–benefit analysis?

options.A: the cost of a ticket for a passenger to travel on a cruise ship
options.B: the cost of fuel to operate the cruise ships
options.C: the costs paid by cruise ships when they dock at the port
options.D: the cost to a fishing fleet of relocating to another port

questions.questionText: Some multinational oil companies extracting oil in developing countries are now required to repair the damage they do to the environment. What best describes the total costs incurred by the oil companies in such circumstances?

options.A: external costs
options.B: private costs plus external costs
options.C: social costs plus external costs
options.D: social costs plus private costs

questions.questionText: Which statement is not an example of government failure?

options.A: government intervention leading to a less efficient allocation of resources
options.B: government intervention leading to a net loss of economic welfare
options.C: government intervention leading to an increase in consumer surplus
options.D: government intervention leading to social costs exceeding social benefits

options.A: Aggregate demand will increase.
options.B: Employment opportunities will increase.

options.D: Tax revenues will increase.

questions.questionText: Which policy to counter climate change is considered to be regulatory rather than market based?

options.A: the introduction of carbon taxes on pollution
options.B: the operation of tradable pollution permits
options.C: the provision of government subsidies
options.D: the setting of industrial emission standards

questions.questionText: Which cause of economic growth is most likely to ensure that the growth is sustainable?

options.A: deregulation of industrial production that uses mineral resources and fossil fuel
options.B: increased government spending on environmental education, financed through taxes on harmful goods
options.C: increased trade barriers on imports to protect domestic jobs and incomes
options.D: reduced planning regulations to encourage construction in areas of natural beauty

questions.questionText: In all major towns in a country, a government adopts a policy of opening centres where job vacancies are advertised. Which type of unemployment is the government aiming to reduce with this policy?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: regional
options.D: seasonal

options.A: Investment depends on the level of business confidence.
options.B: Investment depends on the level of savings.
options.C: Investment depends on the rate of change in national income.
options.D: Investment depends on the rate of change of interest rates.

options.D: the value of expenditure by households on goods and services in a country
